title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio

reading.body:
The core failure here is a training-data practice: Udio's AI music generation model was alleged to have been trained on copyrighted recordings without authorization. The system was deployed publicly before rights clearances were in place, and the gap between what the model learned from and what it was licensed to use became the basis for multiple lawsuits from major labels and independent artists alike. This is a case of a system used outside the conditions its training implied, specifically generating outputs shaped by protected works whose owners had not consented to that use.

The litigation landscape is layered. Universal Music Group settled and entered a licensing agreement with Udio. Warner Music Group did the same. Sony Music filed a separate lawsuit alleging the use of more than 30,000 recordings, was denied the right to add those recordings to its original case, and then filed a new lawsuit to assert them independently. A copyright class action by independent artists survived a motion to dismiss and was moved to a different jurisdiction. A musicians' union lawsuit against UMG over the settlement terms added another strand of dispute.

What is not established is whether any court has issued a final ruling on liability, whether the training practices alleged by Sony or the independent artists actually occurred as described, and whether the settlements reflect an admission of wrongdoing rather than a commercial resolution.

summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, which had been accused of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence model. The companies have reached licensing agreements, with Udio agreeing to launch a new platform next year that will only use authorized and licensed music. Under the deal, users will be able to create, customize, stream and share music through the platform, and artists who opt in will receive compensation. UMG did not disclose the financial terms of the settlement.

The lawsuit alleged that Udio used famous songs like The Temptations' "My Girl" to train its AI, which then generated similar melodies without permission. Udio's CEO called the settlement a breakthrough moment for uniting artificial intelligence with the music industry while supporting artists. This marks the first major licensing agreement between Udio and a major music label. Additionally, UMG announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.
